intent: Independently verify one separately frozen transport-only recovery attempt without replacing completed model failures or concealing original errors.
implementation_author: coordinating /root agent; auditor did not author recover.cjs
scope: Recovery-helper integrity. Each original run must complete before freezing its recovery arm; final paired comparability and recovery outcomes remain to be verified.
verified: The source must have all expected logical records, pass frozen request/consumer replay validation, use one target attempt and the declared original 180-second timeout.

Retry eligibility is restricted to a single failed provider call with a network error or HTTP429/502/503/504. Eligibility does not inspect semantic grade, agreement, correctness, malformed model output or truncation.
HTTP200 model responses remain evidence even when semantically wrong, truncated or malformed. Permanent HTTP errors are not silently retried by this helper.

The endpoint must match the preserved source calls. Only transport timeout changes to 600 seconds; prompt, provider request bytes, consumer, gold, thresholds, repetitions and cases are inherited unchanged.
Original files remain immutable. The recovery manifest preserves every original source path/hash/generation identity and full prior call, including failed transport evidence.

All completed records are copied with source evidence, including semantic and output-contract failures. Canonical alias failures omit the corresponding aliases so the one new canonical call can be reused only within that repetition.
A transport failure in a propagated sequence is rejected rather than silently recovering with a different state trajectory.

The resulting shared runner performs at most one new call for each omitted independent request. Further recovery of a 600-second recovery arm is rejected by this helper's required 180-second source protocol.

Both original and cleaned arms must receive the same declared recovery policy and timeout before refine.cjs comparison; their prompts remain the only provider-request factor between those paired arms.

thinking-baseline-20261015-01.observed_error_type: Client operation aborted due to timeout

thinking-candidate02-20261015-01.status: Still running at inspection; these counts are provisional and cannot supply a complete recovery freeze.

tests.parent_report: Structural transport-classification test passed before audit.
tests.auditor_review: Inspected classification predicate, freeze guards, alias omission, source provenance and manifest preservation; independently counted observed transport errors without model calls.

reporting_requirements: Report original-run transport failures separately from recovery results. A recovered valid output does not retroactively establish first-attempt validity.

Report the number of additional independent retry calls, their outcomes and original source error links. Total original-plus-recovery attempts exceed the recovered run's 348 associated canonical evidence calls by the number of retries.

The shared runner's actual_provider_calls field counts calls attached to retained final records; copied source records and retries require recovery-manifest accounting to describe actual new and cumulative attempts accurately.
Preserve any failed recovery, semantic failure, malformed response or truncation. Do not repeat recovery to obtain a better answer.
Apply complete per-partition, pair, classification and non-regression gates to final paired evidence, while retaining original transport error counts and both timeout policies.
Acceptance remains pending human label review and independent unseen validation; no production timeout or reasoning configuration is adopted by this diagnostic.
limits: A transport retry may yield a new generation; it is permitted because the original request had no consumable provider response, not because the original semantic outcome was unfavorable.
This audit does not preapprove recovery of propagated-sequence failures or any change to provider request bytes.
The clear verdict applies only to the inspected helper hashes and stated one-recovery protocol.
